title: @Hermes @Claude Act as our Master Frontend Designe

msgs.text: @Hermes @Claude Act as our Master Frontend Designer. Stop making generic AI-slop pages with purple gradients and random emojis. From now on, your web builds must strictly adhere to the Agent OS Design Kit specs:  1. GLOBAL FONTS: Always include these typography rules in the HTML <head> (or via an @import in a <style> block if page builders strip links): - 'Bricolage Grotesque' (Weights 700-800) for all primary structural headlines. - 'Manrope' for all clean, readable body text. - 'Caveat' for the signature gold handwritten script (used for eyebrows, quotes, and frameworks).  2. HOUSE STATE PALETTE: - Background: #15101a (Deep Aubergine) - Panels/Cards: #1c1622 or #251d2c - Primary Text: #f3ebda (Cream) - Accent Brand Color: #d4a574 (Gold) - Comparison States: Use #c97c5e (Rust/Coral) for Old/Wrong states vs #5ab896 (Emerald/Teal) for New/Right states.  3. RICH SECTION SKELETON: When I ask you to build a page, you must compose it using a single self-contained HTML page linking 'guide.css' and matching this layout order exactly: - .sticky-banner (With a pinned .banner-cta button) - .hero (With a Caveat eyebrow framework name, two-tone cream + gold <span> headline, and 3 stats) - .source-quote (An italicized reframe line with Caveat attribution) - Section I (The Problem — described in plain English) - Section II (What's Different — including a large .pull quote) - Section III (The Framework — 3 .surface-card moves featuring an emoji + punchy action verb) - Section IV (Setup/Installation — clean bullet list) - Section V & VI (Demos — one showing a vivid data win, one transparently showing limits to build trust) - .agentos-cta (2-column conversion band) - Section VII (The Metrics / Unhyped proof) - Section VIII (Belief-Breakers — 4 .belief blocks showing .wrong vs .right + emerald proof callout) - Section IX (30-Day Roadmap — 4 .roadmap-row phases spanning Days 1-3 to 21-30) - Section X & .final-cta (2 tight closing paragraphs + final closing card + footer)  4. COPYWRITING LAWS: Write in plain, punchy English that a smart 12-year-old can easily understand. Absolutely zero business jargon. Every sentence on its own line during drafts. Never build flat data tables; map details into responsive grids and beautiful cards instead.  Acknowledge that you have locked these design skills into your shared workspace memory.
